document.title: [Bug]: FlashMLA sparse decode allocates the split-KV workspace again on SM90 (regression of #53413)
document.body:
### Your current environment

H200 NVL, vLLM nightly `0bfc7a15d` (FlashMLA pin `0eee43b`), torch 2.13.0+cu130.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

#53413 (runtime OOM in `flash_mla_cuda.sparse_decode_fwd` on H200, fp8 mixed-batch path) was closed by #53755, which pulled in vllm-project/FlashMLA#19: the split-KV accumulators are only allocated when `num_sm_parts > 1`, and the no-split call returns before the combine.

The V4.1 sync, vllm-project/FlashMLA#20 (`c112cc1`), dropped that guard. `csrc/api/sparse_decode.cpp` now allocates `o_accum` and `lse_accum` under `if (enable_split_kv)`, with

```cpp
// Split-KV only pays off when a request has enough work. The sm90 kernel always splits.
bool enable_split_kv = arch.is_sm90a() || !(topk + extra_topk <= 640);
```

vLLM picked this up with the pin bump in #56893, so on Hopper the mixed-batch call again allocates a buffer that grows linearly with `--max-num-batched-tokens`.

Measured on one H200 NVL: a single `flash_mla_with_kvcache` call in the mixed-batch layout (`b=1`, `s_q=T`, `h_q=64`, top-k 2048, `fp8_ds_mla` cache), transient allocation during the call on top of inputs and outputs:

| T | workspace | out + lse |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 256.5 MiB | 64.2 MiB |
| 8192 | 2052 MiB | 514 MiB |
| 32768 | 8208 MiB | 2056 MiB |

That is exactly `(b + num_sm_parts) * s_q * h_q * d_v * 4` bytes with `num_sm_parts = 1`, the case #19 skipped. With the #53413 config (`--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`) every call again needs 8 GiB in one piece, which startup profiling does not see.

Our production image predates #56893, so we have not hit this in serving; we found it while reviewing #58985 and then measured it.

Restoring the `num_sm_parts > 1` guard for SM90 looks like the direct fix, unless the SM90 kernel now needs the accumulators even without a split. A vLLM-side chunking of the mixed batch (#49357) was closed in favour of that kernel fix.

cc @MatthewBonanni @zyongye

<details>
<summary>Measurement script</summary>

```python
import torch

from vllm.v1.attention.ops.flashmla import flash_mla_with_kvcache, get_mla_metadata

BLK, NB, TOPK, D, DV, H = 64, 4096, 2048, 576, 512, 64
cache = torch.zeros(NB, BLK, 1, 656, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")

for T in (1024, 8192, 32768):
    q = torch.randn(T, H, D, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    idx = torch.randint(0, NB * BLK, (1, T, TOPK), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
    seqlens = torch.full((1,), NB * BLK, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    block_table = torch.zeros((1, 1), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    before = torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    out, lse = flash_mla_with_kvcache(
        q=q.unsqueeze(0), k_cache=cache, block_table=block_table, head_dim_v=DV,
        cache_seqlens=seqlens, tile_scheduler_metadata=get_mla_metadata()[0],
        is_fp8_kvcache=True, indices=idx, softmax_scale=D**-0.5,
    )
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    results = out.numel() * out.element_size() + lse.numel() * lse.element_size()
    ws = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() - before - results
    print(f"T={T}: workspace {ws / 2**20:.1f} MiB")
```

</details>

AI assistance was used for this investigation.
